claims.statement: Provider selection is centralized in internal/adapter/provider/resolve.go: Resolve(name) dispatches "github" and "gitlab" to the concrete adapters and rejects any other name with an error naming the supported list, and the package lives in the adapter layer so internal/core never imports concrete provider implementations — core depends only on the port.IssueProvider abstraction.

ReadExecutionIssueSnapshot resolves a provider by name and type-asserts the narrower port.ExecutionIssueSnapshotReader capability, failing closed with distinct errors for unknown provider versus missing reader, and a cancelled context fails before any remote call.

The port.IssueProvider interface normalizes issue, PR/MR, child, body-section, and close operations across gh and glab; every mutating operation requires Confirm=true, and with Confirm=false the adapters return only a redacted dry-run preview without any I/O.

Reconciliation reads providers through read-only candidate search (FindIssueCreateCandidates, ReconcilePullRequest); ReconcilePullRequest results carry AuthoritativeZero so a provably-empty provider inventory is distinguishable from observation failure.

All provider subprocess I/O is bounded by providerutil: 15 s readback timeout, 60 s mutation timeout, 256 KiB output limit, 4096-byte redacted diagnostics, and DryRunPreview redacts argv before rendering a preview.

Created PRs/MRs are verified by readback before the adapter reports success — GitHub and GitLab re-read the created artifact and compare identity, title, body, branches, draft flag, labels, assignees, head SHA, and canonical project; GitLab custom web authorities (explicit port or non-443) additionally require proven glab >= 1.82.0 capability before any mutation.

Per-provider flag-level command details (issue-create recipes, GitHub+Orca linked-branch ordering, GitLab VCS.md snapshot preparation steps) are owned by the operations guide .agent-harness/operations/guides/issueops-providers.md rather than duplicated in code or wiki pages.

GitLab-linked Orca preparation can seal an issue body from a host-observed MCP snapshot: the host agent finds a trusted tool exposing the semantic leaf capability glab_api with a compatible schema (the MCP server namespace and personal wrapper identity are not the capability identity), reads projects/<URL-escaped-project>/issues/<iid>, and supplies exactly provider=gitlab, source=glab_mcp, web_url, body, state via the MCP issueops_execution issue_snapshot input or a 0600 file passed with --issue-snapshot-file.

When no MCP snapshot evidence is supplied, gitlab.Provider.ReadIssueSnapshot reads the same fields through the generic glab api adapter (bounded readback of projects/<escaped>/issues/<iid> --hostname <host>), verifies the returned web_url against the linked issue, and tags the snapshot source=glab_cli; GitHub reads snapshots via gh issue view --json url,body,state with an exact URL match.

The execution adapter injects the snapshot reader per action: executionIssueSnapshotReaderForAction wraps the MCP-evidence reader or the generic fallback, records the resulting source (glab_mcp/glab_cli) into the result, and the MCP-evidence reader re-validates provider, repo, URL, and linked GitLab identity on every call.

GitLab issue snapshot identity is exact and structural — canonical HTTPS authority (lowercased host) plus project path plus positive canonical IID — and /-/issues/:iid and /-/work_items/:iid are the same identity only when all three match; the sealed body must be non-empty and at most 512 KiB and state must be opened or closed.

Supplied issue_snapshot evidence must declare source=glab_mcp; invalid or already-supplied evidence is never re-read via the CLI — preparation fails closed — and the generic glab api adapter is used only when no successful exact-identity MCP evidence existed.

Parent issue and PR/MR creation is intent-first: the core persists a sealed pending intent before the provider call, IssueProviderCreateError.Invoked distinguishes not-started (the only retryable case, by rerunning the exact sealed request) from started, and after invocation a timeout, error, malformed output, failed live verification, or unprojectable canonical number returns a needs-reconciliation, not-retried error instead of success.

Ambiguous provider outcomes are resolved only by the reconcile path: marker-based candidate search must yield exactly one candidate whose title/body digest and live labels/assignees verify before adoption in one CAS; zero or multiple candidates stay blocked, and AuthoritativeZero clears the intent as record cleanup rather than a retry.

Orca is an optional execution adapter — never a native-install dependency and never a second scheduler: native install and self-verify do not require it, and issueops execution prepare --mode auto probes readiness at the pre-mutation boundary resolving to direct whenever Orca is absent or unready; after any possible Orca mutation the durable pending intent and explicit reconcile path are authoritative.

Core — not the Orca adapter — owns the generation-fenced lease, native actor receipt, and canonical CWD fences; the adapter receives the full sealed identity in port.ExecutionOrcaIntentRequest and must treat TerminalHandle as transient observation only, re-resolving it from the persisted worktree ID plus PTY ID because the core never persists it.

internal/adapter/orca is a bounded argv/timeout/envelope projection of the installed orca CLI: fixed argv with path:/id: selectors and single-quoted host commands for codex/claude/omo only, 10 s read / 2 min create / 15 s terminal-close timeouts, 2 MiB envelope and stream limits, and typed port.OrcaError codes with redacted bounded diagnostics that preserve the Invoked flag; the adapter must not duplicate IssueOps state or recovery policy or install Orca.

A non-zero Orca exit that left a well-formed ok:false envelope restores the Orca error code instead of collapsing to command_failed, preserving consumers' not_found idempotent normalization; envelope absence, oversized output, or an ok:true contradiction keep the original failure signal.

The Orca runner retries exactly once without inherited relay environment variables (ORCA_RELAY_DIR, ORCA_RELAY_SOCKET_PATH, ORCA_RELAY_CREDENTIAL_FILE) when the "No owning Orca client is connected to the relay" diagnostic appears, keeping relay identity outside the harness.

Orca readiness probing gates every mutation: it checks the orca binary, runtime/graph ready state, runtime ID resolution, exact repo identity (ID, path match, remote name, worktree base equal to the repo's <repo>.worktrees sibling), per-subcommand help-flag capability checks including provider-specific worktree create flags, host agent model-selection flags (plus codex --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust), and orchestration inventory runtime consistency, returning typed codes rather than partial readiness.

Orca preparation decomposes into six sequential intent stages (worktree_create, terminal_create, run_create, run_bind, task_create, dispatch) persisted by the core before InvokeIntent may run, with strict per-stage receipt monotonicity validated in the adapter; InspectIntent re-reads authoritative Orca inventory per stage and emits candidate inventories with AuthoritativeZero for the reconcile planner.

Orca worktree receipts must match the sealed workspace identity exactly (absolute path, requested branch, sealed base SHA as HEAD, comment marker); GitHub requires a positive linked issue passed as --issue and verifies the receipt's linked issue, while GitLab — whose public Orca CLI has no IID write flag — seals the exact comment marker and cross-checks the native linked-issue field only when observed.

When Orca returns a created branch of exactly <namespace>/<requested>, the adapter renames it with git branch -m and restores the upstream: with a sealed base that is an exact 40/64-hex Git object ID and refs/remotes/origin/<branch> provably resolving to that SHA, the upstream re-attaches to that remote ref (GitLab numeric branch suffixes tolerated only under that proof); otherwise a plain base branch name becomes the upstream — and execution-level tests pin that creation stays pinned to the sealed base without an absent upstream.

Umbrella child cycles seal a canonical parent worktree path and the adapter must prove explicit lineage: lineageConfidence=explicit, lineageSource of explicit-cli-flag (create's --parent-worktree) or manual-action, and an exact repoID::parentPath match; independent cycles create with --no-parent so the Orca UI layer matches IssueOps provider-native parentage.

LaunchOwner chains terminal, Run, bind, task, and dispatch with receipt validation at each hop and dispatches codex/claude with --inject; Omo is deliberately not injected — the adapter validates the dispatch preamble and delivers it as one bracketed-paste terminal send --enter, and reconcile rejects Omo dispatch inspection because prompt delivery is unproven after dispatch.

SendWorkerDone and UpdateTask/SettleTask exist in the Orca adapter but are intentionally not wired into IssueOps completion: execution complete records only a durable lifecycle receipt, and the Orca dispatch's terminal transition belongs to the dispatched owner holding the sealed capability — wiring both would create two competing completion authorities; SettleTask documents the one-shot consumer_fenced recovery via UseRun.

Only normalized DTOs cross internal/port: the issue-snapshot DTO is owned by internal/contract/executionissue and merely re-exported by the port package so the contract layer never imports port, and Orca port DTOs carry runtime IDs and bounded identities but no environment or credential state.

MCP server namespaces and wrapper identity, credential profiles and tokens, Orca relay environment, claim-token file contents (which never enter state, prompts, or logs), and terminal handles as authority all stay outside core — only the normalized provider/source/URL/body/state DTO crosses the port.

Cleanup uses the narrow CleanupOrcaTerminals surface (Status, ListAllTerminals, ListWorktreeTerminalsByPath, CloseTerminal) that closes only the fingerprint-approved exact handle and succeeds only with a PTY-killed receipt, normalizes selector_not_found to "no terminals", and keeps cleanup's terminal needs off the main OrcaClient interface.

cmd/harness/harnessapp is the only place concrete adapters are constructed: productionIssueOpsExecutionDependencies wires orca.NewExecution() as both provisioner and owner inspector and provider.ReadExecutionIssueSnapshot as the snapshot reader, while the execution CLI and MCP facades receive injected handlers and never resolve adapters themselves.

internal/architecture/dependency_test.go enforces the boundary edges: internal/core/issueops must not import internal/adapter/provider, the application layer must not import adapters, and concrete construction (provider.Resolve, orca.NewExecution) outside composition-root preparation wiring is flagged as a violation.

The Orca port owns per-host implementer/planner model defaults applied by execution prepare when --owner-model/--owner-effort are omitted (codex gpt-5.6-terra/xhigh, claude claude-sonnet-5/high, omo openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol/max; planner-grade codex gpt-5.6-sol/xhigh and claude claude-opus-5/high), returning ok=false for unsupported hosts so callers fail closed.
